_meta.voice: Voice v2 — second person, present tense, short declarative lines, dry needle. Needles the choice, never the kid. No corporate softener.
_meta.scope: Activity screens and milestones only. The monthly finance / quiet / runway / year-open / stage-up banks live in lib/engine/log.ts — do not duplicate them here.

placeholders.{cash}: cash on hand after the action, formatted
placeholders.{n}: the number belonging to this action — headcount hired/fired, amount spent, milestone count

company: The company screen. Everything in here changes what {company} is, not just what it earns.
This is where you edit the thing itself. Cheap to tap. Expensive to be wrong about.
Direction, name, product. Choose carefully — the market keeps receipts.
team: Four executive seats. Each one you fill costs payroll and buys judgment you don't have yet.
People are the biggest line in your burn and the only line that can quit.
Hire, fire, promote. Morale is watching all three.
assets: Property and holdings. Things you own that sit still and cost money while they sit.
Cash turned into stuff. Stuff turns back into cash slower than you want it to.
Assets appreciate on the market's schedule, not yours. Runway: {runway}.
market: The market screen. Everyone else is here too, spending more than you.
This is where you rent attention. The rent goes up every year.
Channels, spend, share. You can move CAC or you can move Brand. Rarely both at once.
closet: The closet. None of this touches your books. All of it changes how you walk in.
Clothes don't move a valuation. They move the room, slightly, for about ten seconds.
Pick a look. The panel notices, then goes straight back to your margins.

hire: You add a salary to the burn before you add the revenue. Every founder makes that bet.
{n} more on payroll. Burn: {burn}. They cost you on day one and pay back on a day you can't name.
Headcount up. Runway down to {runway}. Make them worth the months.
One more person who needs you to be right. That's what a team actually is.
fire: You cut a salary out of the burn. Everyone left does the arithmetic on themselves tonight.
The seat is empty. The work isn't. Somebody absorbs it, and it's usually you.
Burn falls to {burn}. Morale falls too. You traded one for the other on purpose.
{n} fewer people. Cheaper company, smaller company. Both true at the same time.
rndSpend: You put {n} into a product that doesn't exist yet. Later is where the good outcomes live.
R&D. The only line item that pays you back in a year you might not reach.
Quality climbs, cash drops to {cash}. The tech debt goes quiet for a while.
You're buying a better version of the thing on credit. Runway: {runway}.
marketingPush: You spend {n} getting strangers to notice. Some will. Fewer will pay.
The push goes out. CAC tells you in a month whether that was marketing or just spending.
Attention costs {n} and expires. Brand is the part that doesn't.
You bought reach. Now find out whether the product deserved it.
propertyBuy: Cash becomes a building. Buildings are patient. Your runway is not.
{n} of square footage. It appreciates slowly and charges rent on your attention.
Cash: {cash}. Part of your company is made of concrete now.
An asset on the books, a hole in the bank. On the right day those are the same sentence.
rename: {company} it is. The leaderboard remembers what you used to be called.
New name, same numbers. The market recognizes you again in about a year.
You rebrand. Nothing on the books moves. That's what vanity costs.

good: Year {year} closes up. Revenue {rev}, valuation {valuation}. Now do it again, larger.
A good year. The books finally agree with the story you've been telling.
You end at {valuation} with {runway} of runway. The panel will expect more, out loud.
Green year. Green years are when founders get careless. Don't.
flat: Year {year} ends about where it started. The market moved. You didn't.
Revenue {rev} against burn {burn}. Nothing broke. Nothing got built either.
You held the line for twelve months. Holding is a pause, not a strategy.
Same valuation, one less year of patience from everyone who funded you.
bad: Year {year} ends down. Valuation {valuation}, runway {runway}. The math is not asking your opinion.
A bad year. Name the three decisions that did it. The autopsy will, eventually.
Revenue {rev} against burn {burn}. You spent twelve months paying for last year's optimism.
The books shrank. Companies don't die of one year like this. They die of two.

chapter7: {company} is out of money. Chapter 7: the court sells what's left and pays whoever it can.
Runway hit zero in year {year}. It was visible from a long way back.
You didn't lose to the market. You lost to a burn rate you kept calling temporary.
The doors close at {valuation}. Everything you built gets sorted into piles and priced.
This is the part that teaches. Read the autopsy — three decisions did most of the damage, and all three are learnable.
ipo: {company} goes public at {valuation}. Strangers own you now, and strangers vote.
Year {year}, from nothing to a ticker. The shark has stopped comparing you to a lemonade stand.
You're public. Every quarter is a pitch from here, and the audience never leaves.
milestone: Milestone logged. The ones you missed are on the same record.
Badge earned in year {year}. Legacy keeps it after this run ends.
You crossed a line most runs never reach. The next line sits further out.
That's {n} on the board. {company} has a history now, and history is what the panel reads first.
